blocks.text: Admach Systems Limited is an engineer-to-order machine builder based at Nandoshi, off Pune Sinhagad Road, Pune. It designs, manufactures and supplies Special Purpose Machines (SPMs), automation systems, assembly and packaging machines, robotic material-handling systems and non-destructive testing (NDT) equipment. [F] (SCREENER) The company was incorporated in 2008. [F] (SCREENER) Its own description of the product set is six categories: SPMs for steel bars (bar handling, chamfering, straightening, peeling, UT check, grinding, finishing); NDT and X-ray systems (magnetic particle inspection, ultrasonic testing, magnetic flux leakage, X-ray inspection, customised testing cabinets); pipe solutions (SAW pipe cleaning, internal/external welding, handling modules, radiography); handling and packaging for bars and coils; billet conditioning lines for alloy steel; and general steel-industry equipment (cooling beds, shears, conveyors, bundle transfer). [F] (PPT Jun 2026)

It makes money by selling individual custom-built machines and complete lines against purchase orders, on a milestone payment structure: **20% advance, 70% on equipment readiness and customer inspection at the Pune factory, 10% after installation at the customer site**, with government orders typically carrying no advance and 80-90% on inspection. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Feb 2026) Revenue is recognised on invoicing at dispatch; until dispatch, accumulated cost sits in inventory. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) Average project cycle is 3.5-4 months, ranging from 2.5 months for a single X-ray cabinet to 6-7 months for a complete line, with 20-25 projects on the shop floor at any time. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) After-sales maintenance, repair and technical support are also offered. [F] (PPT Jun 2026)

End markets as the company names them are steel and mining, defence, nuclear and atomic energy, aerospace, automobile, food processing, tooling and advanced engineering. [F] (PPT Jun 2026) **A percentage split by end market is disclosed only as a chart in the investor presentation whose data labels cannot be reliably matched to years or categories in the text version available to us, so we do not reproduce it.** The only numeric end-market splits we can cite are verbal and mutually inconsistent: about 50% of business from special-grade steel processing equipment and 30% from NDT and defence combined [MC] (CALL Feb 2026); defence plus nuclear at 10-15% of H1 FY26 revenue [MC] (CALL Feb 2026); and an analyst's assertion on the FY26 call that defence is 'just 5% of our current revenues', which management did not correct but also did not confirm numerically [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Within steel, management puts 70-75% of steel revenue in long products and 25-30% in flat products. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Geography is overwhelmingly domestic but shifting. The presentation's geography chart shows domestic/international at 99.81/0.19 in FY23, 99.94/0.06 in FY24, 92.38/7.16 in FY25 and 87.39/12.61 in FY26. [F] (PPT Jun 2026) (The FY25 column sums to 99.54 rather than 100 in our copy; we have not reconciled that.) Management separately said on the FY26 call that the company works '95% of the times for local market in India'. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) Export country count is stated three different ways within five months: 26+ countries in the presentation dated 25 May 2026 [F] (PPT Jun 2026), 27 countries on the January 2026 call [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), and 'over 28 countries' on the 28 May 2026 call [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

Customer profile is large industrial buyers and European machine-building partners: Tata Steel, NMDC Steel, Nuclear Fuel Complex, Blue Star, Kalyani Hospet, ArcelorMittal DSTCFZE (UAE), Indian Ordnance Factories, and six European technology partners through whom a meaningful part of the export business is routed. [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) **No customer concentration figure - top 1, top 5 or top 10 - is disclosed anywhere in the evidence available.** That is a finding, not an omission on our side.

Listing status and what it does to the evidence base: Admach listed on the BSE SME platform (scrip code 544669) on 31 December 2025 at an issue price of Rs 239, opened at Rs 191.20 below issue price and closed its debut at Rs 200.75. [F] (BOARD) As an SME-platform issuer it reports half-yearly, not quarterly, so our statements data contains only four reported half-year periods (H1 FY25 to H2 FY26), not a twelve-quarter series. [F] (NUMBERS) The FY26 annual report was filed on 31 August 2026 [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS) but its text is not in our evidence set, and no prospectus or RHP is available to us. Consequently there is no auditor's report, no key audit matters, no CARO observations, no contingent liability schedule, no related-party transaction schedule, no segment margin disclosure and no customer concentration data in this report. Every conclusion below is drawn from two earnings calls, one investor presentation, four exchange announcements, a screener profile and the statements data.

blocks.text: **Classifying the drivers.** Structural: import substitution against European SPM builders, Indian defence indigenisation and the nuclear build-out, and the European partnership channel (rows 4, 5, 6). Company-specific and within management's control: the debt-free balance sheet, backward integration, capacity headroom and export mix (rows 1, 2, 3, 7). Cyclical: the steel capex cycle, which management itself describes as the source of roughly half of revenue and which drives row 8 [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). **The two drivers that matter most to the price - defence/nuclear scale-up and margin expansion - are the two with the weakest evidence today** [AI].

subsections.title: Bear thesis - the strongest reasons not to own it

items: **1. Profit does not turn into cash.** Operating cash flow was -0.58x reported profit over the last three years and -0.74x over five [F] (NUMBERS). FY26 CFO was -Rs 4.53 cr against PAT of Rs 10.01 cr [F] (PPT Jun 2026). Free cash flow was negative in all five years; cumulative five-year FCF is -Rs 37 cr [F] (NUMBERS). A company that has never generated free cash in its disclosed history is being valued as if it will.

**2. Working capital is moving the wrong way, fast.** Working-capital days 231 in FY26 against an 89-day prior average; cash conversion cycle 322 days; debtor days 166 against a 90-day three-year average [F] (NUMBERS). Receivables went Rs 4.82 cr (FY24) to Rs 18.37 cr (FY25) to Rs 31.32 cr (FY26) while revenue went Rs 19.68 cr to Rs 53.36 cr to Rs 68.91 cr - receivables grew 6.5x while revenue grew 3.5x [F] (PPT Jun 2026). Management guides to about 75 working-capital days in FY27 [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), a three-fold improvement in one year that nothing in the record supports [AI].

**3. The margin story is going backwards, not forwards.** Gross margin on our reconstruction of the company's own P&L was about 54.5% in FY24, 31.1% in FY25 and 30.3% in FY26 [E] (PPT Jun 2026). Operating margin excluding other income was 23.5% in H1 FY26 and 15.1% in H2 FY26 - an 840 basis point sequential fall [E] (NUMBERS) (PPT Jun 2026) - in the same half in which the backward-integration equipment was being installed. The FY24 operating margin of 32% was a single-project artefact, which the Company Secretary effectively conceded: 'in year 2024 the major customer is from steel sector, that is Tata Steel. The major profitability is coming from that project.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

**4. FY26 profit was flattered below the operating line.** The H2 FY26 current tax charge was Rs 53.24 lakh on PBT of Rs 606.53 lakh, an 8.8% rate, against 20.6% in H2 FY25 [F] (PPT Jun 2026). An analyst pressed twice; management gave two different explanations (accelerated depreciation under the Income Tax Act, then 'we have the benefit for six months'), conceded that depreciation was flat half on half, and the question was left unresolved [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Other income of Rs 93.04 lakh was 7.7% of FY26 PBT, of which Rs 86.34 lakh landed in H2 [F] (PPT Jun 2026). Together, the lower tax rate versus FY25 and other income account for roughly Rs 1.7 cr, or about 17%, of FY26 reported PAT [E] (PPT Jun 2026).

**5. The price already assumes an outcome larger than anything management has claimed.** The reverse DCF implies about 56.8% sales CAGR for five years against a base-case equivalent of 19.8% [F] (NUMBERS). Compounded off FY26 revenue of Rs 68.91 cr, that is roughly Rs 654 cr of revenue by FY31 [E] (NUMBERS) - about 3.3x the Rs 200 cr that management says is the maximum the existing facility can support, and 3.3x the Rs 200 cr aspiration they set for FY28 [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

**6. The order book is shrinking and is reported inconsistently.** Rs 76.95 cr in January 2026 [MC] (CALL Feb 2026); approximately Rs 65 cr in the May 2026 presentation and call [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026); 'order book rises to Rs 83.77 crore' on 16 July 2026; 'order book rises to Rs 68.37 crore' on 18 August 2026 [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS). **Two consecutive press releases both say the book 'rises to' a figure, the second Rs 15.40 cr below the first.** These are not reconciled in any document available to us.

**7. Customer concentration is entirely undisclosed, in a business that was recently single-customer dependent.** No top-1/5/10 revenue share appears in any document. As recently as FY24, management describes Tata Steel as 'the major customer' carrying 'the major profitability' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). On the FY26 call, a single machine awaiting dispatch was worth Rs 15-16 cr - about 22% of full-year FY26 revenue [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [E]. That is the concentration risk made visible by accident.

**8. Institutions left within one quarter of listing.** FII holding fell from 2.83% to 1.06% and DII holding from 7.95% to 1.00% between December 2025 and March 2026; public holding rose from 36.26% to 44.98%; the number of shareholders fell from 958 to 417 [F] (NUMBERS). Roughly 8.7 percentage points of institutional stock, about 5.9 lakh shares, changed hands into retail within one quarter of listing [E] (NUMBERS).

**9. Liquidity is a hard constraint, not a soft one.** Same-day traded turnover was reported at about Rs 25.21 lakh on 17 August 2026 [F] (BOARD). At that level, position sizing - not the thesis - governs whether the name is investable for most institutional accounts.

**10. The disclosure record contains arithmetic that does not hold.** In the investor presentation, the FY24 cash-flow column shows operating, investing and financing flows summing to +Rs 15.96 cr against a stated net decrease in cash of Rs 0.88 lakh; the FY25 and FY26 columns reconcile exactly [F] (PPT Jun 2026). The same presentation shows FY24 EPS of Rs 7.45, which cannot be derived from its own FY24 PAT of Rs 334.81 lakh and FY24 share capital of Rs 200.00 lakh (Rs 16.74 on those inputs) [E] (PPT Jun 2026). The presentation also states '17+ Year in Business' on one page and '29+ years of expertise' on another [F] (PPT Jun 2026).

**11. The evidence base itself is a risk.** No annual report text, no prospectus, no auditor's report, no CARO, no contingent liabilities, no related-party schedule, no segment margins, half-yearly reporting only, and shareholding data that stops at March 2026 [F] (NUMBERS). Underwriting this name today means underwriting management's word on most of what matters [AI].

subsections.title: Key debates - what the market may be getting wrong, both ways

blocks.caption: Three debates that determine the outcome
rows: Is the working-capital drain structural or a timing accident?

Management attributes it to shipping and container unavailability from 'recent international chaos', with machines inspected, paid-for on arrival at Bombay port and rerouted via South Africa; transport cost is on the customer's account [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). If so, FY27 CFO turns positive and the DCF's 151-day working-capital assumption is achievable.

Debtor days have risen every single year for five years - 36, 55, 89, 126, 166 - through periods with no shipping disruption at all [F] (NUMBERS). A monotonic five-year trend is not a one-off. Payable days simultaneously collapsed from 162 to 59 [F] (NUMBERS), meaning the company is now financing both sides of the cycle.
H1 FY27 (September 2026 half) receivables and CFO. Debtor days below 120 and positive CFO would support management; another rise settles it against them.
Is the defence and nuclear exposure a business or a narrative?

The company has supplied testing machines for bomb shells and missile bodies to Indian Ordnance Factories and exported through partners to government buyers in Korea, Brazil and Taiwan; it holds a live Rs 10 cr NFC order with four to eight similar projects at technical-offer stage [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Genuine qualification into these supply chains is not easily replicated.

On management's own numbers, defence plus nuclear was 10-15% of H1 FY26 revenue, and the single largest piece of the order book attributable to defence was Rs 10-15 cr of a Rs 76 cr book [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). The presentation devotes several pages to India's defence and nuclear TAM but the company's actual exposure is small, project-based and lumpy [AI].

Disclosure of a segment revenue split that management promised to circulate 'in another week's time' on 28 May 2026 [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) and which is not in any document available to us; plus whether the 155 mm howitzer orders convert.
Does backward integration create margin, or just absorb capital?

Rs 18 cr of FY26 capex and Rs 11.44 cr of CWIP bring laser cutting, press braking, tapping and CNC machining in-house, flipping outsourcing from 70% to 30% and saving vendor payouts, transportation and coordination; management sizes the benefit at 3-4 points of EBITDA margin [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

Capex was 26.1% of FY26 sales [F] (NUMBERS), CWIP at year end was 2.3x the entire net block [F] (PPT Jun 2026), and the half in which the machines were installed delivered the lowest operating margin in two years [E] (NUMBERS). In-sourcing also converts variable cost into fixed cost, which raises the downside in a lumpy order business [AI].
H1 FY27 operating margin against the 23.5% H1 FY26 comparator, and whether CWIP of Rs 11.44 cr capitalises into the block and starts earning.

items: **A fourth debate, smaller but live:** whether the Rs 200 cr capacity claim is credible. The company told the market in its RHP that it was operating at 100% capacity utilisation, then said one additional shed gave 'additional 40% expansion potential' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), then said the same facility can support Rs 200 cr [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Starting from FY25 revenue of Rs 53 cr, 100% utilisation plus 40% implies roughly Rs 75 cr, not Rs 200 cr [E]. Management's own capacity arithmetic does not close [AI].

**A fifth:** whether the European partnerships are an asset or a dependency. They supply the technology, several of the export orders and the credibility with large industrial clients [F] (PPT Jun 2026). No agreement term, exclusivity, notice period or partner-routed revenue share is disclosed anywhere. A partner switching to a different Indian integrator is an unquantifiable risk today [AI].

blocks.text: The consensus read of Admach - to the extent 417 shareholders constitute a consensus - is an import-substituting defence and nuclear precision-engineering play with 29% revenue growth, 59% profit growth, zero debt and a Rs 65-84 cr order book. Our variant perception is that **the accounting profit and the cash economics have separated, and the market is pricing the accounting profit.** Over FY24-FY26 the company reported Rs 19.66 cr of cumulative PAT and generated cumulative operating cash flow of roughly -Rs 11 cr [E] (NUMBERS) (PPT Jun 2026); the entire net IPO proceeds of about Rs 38.35 cr [E] (PPT Jun 2026) were absorbed by capex of Rs 18 cr, debt repayment of Rs 10.66 cr, a Rs 8.59 cr reduction in trade payables and a Rs 12.95 cr increase in receivables, leaving Rs 4.52 cr of cash at year end [F] (PPT Jun 2026). That is not a fraud signal; it is what a growing engineer-to-order business with 322-day cash conversion looks like. But it means the correct question is not 'how fast can revenue grow' but 'how much capital does each rupee of growth consume' - and at 231 working-capital days, growth is cash-destructive at the current cycle. The second element of the variant view is that the market is capitalising a defence and nuclear narrative that is, on the company's own disclosure, 10-15% of revenue [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), against a price that requires 56.8% compound sales growth for five years [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: The statements data is explicitly prepared on a **standalone** basis and no consolidated statements are referenced anywhere [F] (NUMBERS). The absence of any named subsidiary is consistent with a single-entity, single-site operating company, but we cannot confirm it: the annual report, which would carry the AOC-1 and the related-party schedule, is not in our evidence set. The only group-level asset flagged in the record is **land adjacent to the factory that is held in the promoter's name, which management said 'can be transferred to the company'** [MC] (CALL Feb 2026); no transfer, valuation or consideration has been disclosed since.

The company is 18 years old; **the business being valued is about three years old.** Revenue was Rs 14 cr in FY22 and Rs 13 cr in FY23 - it went backwards - before Rs 20 cr in FY24, Rs 53 cr in FY25 and Rs 69 cr in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). Roughly 81% of FY26 revenue was added in the three years to March 2026 [E] (NUMBERS). Every one of the six European partnerships that underpins the technology narrative is dated 2020 or later, and three of the six date from 2025 [F] (PPT Jun 2026). The defence and nuclear exposure that dominates the investor presentation is evidenced only from 2024 onwards [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

This matters for two reasons. First, the long-cycle claims - '13 long-term clients with 15+ year relationships' [F] (PPT Jun 2026), 'we are working in the defense sector for almost 20 years now' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) - describe a period in which the company was doing Rs 13-14 cr of revenue. Relationship longevity at Rs 13 cr of revenue is weak evidence of relationship durability at Rs 200 cr [AI]. Second, there is no disclosed operating history through a downturn at the current scale: the only contraction in the record, FY22 to FY23, happened at a revenue base one fifth of today's [F] (NUMBERS).

The pre-IPO capital history is not disclosed in our evidence set. Share capital went Rs 0.21 cr (FY22) to Rs 1.00 cr (FY23) to Rs 2.00 cr (FY24) to Rs 4.99 cr (FY25) to Rs 6.77 cr (FY26) [F] (NUMBERS) (PPT Jun 2026). Reconciling the FY25 movement in total equity (Rs 5.73 cr to Rs 22.07 cr) against FY25 PAT of Rs 6.30 cr, financing cash flow of +Rs 3.51 cr, debt repayment of Rs 4.93 cr and interest of Rs 1.70 cr implies roughly Rs 10.1 cr of pre-IPO equity raised in cash during FY25 [E] (PPT Jun 2026). The allottees, price and terms of that pre-IPO issuance are not disclosed in any document available to us.

sections.title: Business model, value chain and capital intensity

subsections.title: The production chain, step by step

items: **Step 1 - Concept and quotation.** Management characterises the model as 'concept selling', not product selling: 'This is tailor-made equipment... if my concept is liked by the customer, he does not even go for the second quotation also.' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) Quotations outstanding were stated at approximately Rs 200 cr in both January and May 2026 [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Jun 2026).

**Step 2 - Order and advance.** Private and steel customers pay a 20% advance at order; government customers typically pay no advance [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Customer advances stood at Rs 9.74 cr at 31 March 2026, within Rs 10.84 cr of other current liabilities [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [F] (PPT Jun 2026).

**Step 3 - Design and approval (roughly the first month).** 'For first one month only engineering is happening. So, no physical money payout is happening.' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) This is where the application engineering and design validation the company claims as a barrier actually sits [F] (PPT Jun 2026).

**Step 4 - Procurement.** Bought-in components include Siemens drives and geared motors on 30-60 day, occasionally 90-day, vendor credit [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Until the FY26 capex, 70% of component work was outsourced to job workers and 30% done in-house [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

**Step 5 - Fabrication, machining, welding, assembly.** Performed in-house across three assembly halls at Nandoshi, Pune [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [F] (PPT Jun 2026). The FY26 capex - CNC laser cutting, CNC press brake, automatic tapping and CNC machining - is intended to flip the outsourcing ratio to 30% outsourced / 70% in-house [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

**Step 6 - Testing, multi-stage QC and customer inspection at the factory.** The customer inspects at Pune; on acceptance, 70% of the contract value falls due (80-90% for government orders) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

**Step 7 - Dispatch and invoicing.** Revenue is recognised only on invoice at dispatch: 'Once it is dispatched, invoice is generated, then that figure gets transmitted to the revenue books... Till that time, it will show as inventory.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) This is the mechanical reason inventory and the revenue line are so tightly coupled, and why a shipping delay converts directly into a revenue deferral.
**Step 8 - Site installation and commissioning.** The final 10% is released after installation at the customer's site [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

subsections.title: Where value is captured, and why

blocks.text: Management's own thumb rule locates the value capture precisely. For a 1 million tonne per annum long-products plant costing Rs 5,000-6,000 cr, the rolling mill is roughly Rs 400-500 cr, and Admach's post-rolling scope - finishing, inspection and packaging - is Rs 40-50 cr, i.e. about 10% of the rolling mill and under 1% of the total plant capex [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Billet conditioning, upstream of rolling, adds another Rs 30-40 cr of potential scope [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). **The company sits in a narrow, late, high-specification slice of the steel capex chain.** That slice is defensible because it is engineering-intensive and low-volume, which is exactly why global majors do not chase it; it is also small, which is why the addressable value per plant is bounded regardless of how much steel capacity India builds [AI].

In NDT and defence the capture point is different: the company is a qualified supplier of inspection equipment into supply chains where failure tolerance is near zero, and where a Make-in-India 50% local-content requirement pushes European principals to bid jointly with an Indian integrator rather than directly [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Value is captured through qualification and through being the partner of choice for the European principal - not through proprietary technology, which the partners hold [AI]. This is a real but conditional position: it depends on the partner relationships, none of whose commercial terms are disclosed.

Management claims a 30-40% price advantage over European competitors [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). If that is accurate, the company's gross margin of roughly 30% in FY25 and FY26 [E] (PPT Jun 2026) suggests the advantage is being passed to the customer rather than retained - which is consistent with winning share but not with expanding margin. We cannot verify the 30-40% claim from any document.

The presentation describes the company as operating 'on an asset-light model, with capacity primarily driven by order flow and working capital availability' and promises 'modular capacity enabling scalable volumes with minimal incremental capex' [F] (PPT Jun 2026). **The FY26 numbers contradict the label.** Capex was Rs 18 cr, or 26.1% of sales [F] (NUMBERS); CWIP at 31 March 2026 was Rs 11.44 cr against a net block of Rs 4.94 cr [F] (PPT Jun 2026); investing cash outflow was Rs 19.19 cr [F] (PPT Jun 2026). Fixed-asset turnover remains high at 13.8x [F] (NUMBERS), so the fixed-asset side is genuinely light - but the working-capital side is not.

The correct description is **working-capital-heavy rather than fixed-asset-heavy.** At 31 March 2026, inventories of Rs 28.24 cr and receivables of Rs 31.32 cr together were Rs 59.56 cr, or 65.3% of total assets of Rs 91.19 cr, against hard assets (PPE plus CWIP plus intangibles) of Rs 16.42 cr, or 18.0% [E] (PPT Jun 2026). The company's own statement that capacity is 'driven by order flow and working capital availability' is the accurate half of the sentence; 'asset-light' is the misleading half [AI]. Management's claim that Rs 200 cr of revenue would need only Rs 20-30 cr of working capital [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) implies 36-55 working-capital days, against the 231 days actually run in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: **Genuinely differentiated:** NDT and X-ray systems for mission-critical applications. The specification is written by the end-use standard, the supplier has to be qualified, and the customer cannot easily swap vendors mid-programme. The company's own example - X-raying a fully assembled, fuzed 155 mm howitzer shell in continuous mode on a 12-axis servo gantry with microfocus and 450 kV tubes [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) - is a genuinely narrow capability. Billet conditioning lines are similarly differentiated but explicitly dependent on Braun Maschinenfabrik [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

**Commodity-like:** cooling beds, shears, conveyors, bundle transfer and packaging modules. These are fabrication-and-integration products where the barrier is price and delivery, not technology. The company does not disclose what share of revenue they represent. Given that management puts roughly 50% of business in special-grade steel processing equipment [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), and that steel processing lines bundle differentiated inspection modules with commodity handling modules, **it is likely that a material part of revenue is fabrication-led rather than technology-led** [AI]. This is the single most important undisclosed mix question in the business.

The one durable-technology test the documents allow: management states that in NDT, equipment life is shortened by changing standards - 'once the standard is changing, you have to change the equipment' - versus 15-20 year equipment life in steel [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). That is a favourable replacement-cycle claim for the NDT line. It is also unquantified: no installed base, no spares revenue, no replacement order has ever been disclosed.

subsections.title: Is the export shift strategy or mix?

blocks.text: **Both, but mostly mix so far.** The evidence for strategy: the company has had European partners since 2020, added Italian and Austrian clients in 2025, and the MD describes a deliberate 'Phase 2' in which the partnerships convert from inbound technology into outbound distribution - 'currently, we are working 95% of the times for local market in India. And the next phase will be with this partnership... we will start exporting also' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The evidence for mix: exports were 0.06% of FY24 revenue and 12.61% of FY26 [F] (PPT Jun 2026); a shift of that speed off a near-zero base is the arrival of a handful of projects, not a channel build. Specific identified export clusters - six US pipe projects, a Brazil howitzer system of about Rs 2 cr, Korea and Taiwan missile-shell systems - are individually small and individually lumpy [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Feb 2026).

There is also a routing question the documents do not resolve. Several export deliveries are described as 'exported through Indian Partner' in the product table [F] (PPT Jun 2026), and management describes exporting both directly and through Nordinkraft [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). **What share of the 12.61% international revenue is direct versus partner-intermediated is not disclosed.** That distinction determines whether the export margin premium management claims accrues to Admach or to the partner [AI].

items: **Currency exposure is not disclosed.** No hedging policy, forward book, foreign-currency receivable or payable balance, or currency-wise revenue split appears in any document available to us. **Make in India / local content.** Management states a 50% local-content requirement on the nuclear work, which is what pushes European principals to bid jointly rather than directly [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). This is a favourable policy exposure, and also a dependency: it is the policy, not the technology, that creates the partnering incentive [AI].

**Tariff exposure is not disclosed.** No document available to us discusses import duties on components, export duties, anti-dumping exposure, or US or EU tariff treatment of the company's products. Given six live US projects [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), this is a meaningful gap.

blocks.text: **Where the company sits in the value chain.** Admach is a capital-equipment supplier to defence and nuclear manufacturers, not a defence manufacturer. subsections.title: Aggregate utilisation and why it moved

blocks.text: **No utilisation percentage is disclosed for any year.** The only utilisation statements in the record are these three, and they do not sit together. First, the RHP stated that the company was operating at 100% capacity utilisation - put to management by an analyst in January 2026 and not disputed [MC] (CALL Feb 2026); on FY25 revenue that implies a ceiling of about Rs 53 cr. Second, management said that after building one additional assembly shed, 'that gives us additional 40% expansion potential' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) - which takes the implied ceiling to roughly Rs 75 cr [E]. Third, management says the same facility can support Rs 200 cr [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Jun 2026).

**Management's own capacity arithmetic does not close.** 100% utilisation at roughly Rs 53 cr, plus 40%, is roughly Rs 75 cr - not Rs 200 cr [E]. FY26 revenue of Rs 68.91 cr implies utilisation of about 92% on the first basis and about 34% on the second [E]. The two readings imply completely different capital requirements for the next Rs 100 cr of revenue, and the documents do not reconcile them. This is the single most consequential unresolved operational question in the file.

What we can say with confidence: physical space is not the binding constraint. Only 28,925 sq ft of 75,347 sq ft of land is utilised [F] (PPT Jun 2026), management holds adjacent land for Units 2 and 3, and the presentation itself describes capacity as 'primarily driven by order flow and working capital availability' [F] (PPT Jun 2026). **On the company's own account, the binding constraints are orders and working capital, not machinery or floor space** - which is consistent with a 231-day working-capital cycle [F] (NUMBERS) and an order book that has fallen over seven months [AI].

blocks.text: **Thirteen inconsistencies across four documents covering seven months is a high count for a company of this size.** Individually most are explicable - rounding conventions, chart artefacts, weighted-average share counts, different as-of dates. Collectively they describe a reporting function that is not yet operating to listed-company standard: the FY24 cash-flow column does not balance, the FY24 EPS cannot be derived from the company's own inputs, and two consecutive press releases publish contradictory order-book figures. **We treat this as a disclosure-quality finding, not as evidence of misstatement in the audited FY26 numbers, which internally reconcile.**

The headline is that working-capital days rose to 231 in FY26 from 111 in FY25 and an 89-day average over the prior three years [F] (NUMBERS), while the cash conversion cycle is 322 days [F] (NUMBERS). **Both figures are true and both are misleading on their own,** for three reasons. First, revenue recognition happens at dispatch, so a machine finished and customer-inspected but stuck for want of a vessel sits in inventory and inflates the denominatorless side of every ratio without any commercial problem existing [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Second, the FY24 statements-data figures - inventory days of 1,942, payable days of 771 and a cash conversion cycle of 1,260 days [F] (NUMBERS) - are distorted by a tiny cost denominator against a large inventory build and should not be read as literal descriptions of that year [AI]. Third, the cycle is structurally long by design: a 20/70/10 milestone structure with a 3.5-7 month build means the company is meant to hold work in progress [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

**What is not explained away by any of that is the direction of the components.** Debtor days have risen in every single one of the last five years - 36, 55, 89, 126, 166 - and payable days have collapsed from 162 to 59 in one year [F] (NUMBERS). A monotonic five-year receivable trend is a structural fact, not a shipping accident [AI].

blocks.text: A second, sharper contradiction sits in the January 2026 call. Asked whether working capital was blocked for six to nine months per order, the Executive Director replied 'our investment cycle will be somewhere around 60 days, not more than that', and separately said of European partners 'We never block our money with anybody' [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). **Against a reported cash conversion cycle of 322 days and 231 working-capital days [F] (NUMBERS), the 60-day claim is not reconcilable with the accounts.** Management may be describing net cash investment per project rather than balance-sheet working capital, but no such distinction was drawn, and the two statements are presented to investors as descriptions of the same thing [AI].

items: **The direct consequence:** FY26 CFO of -Rs 4.53 cr against PAT of Rs 10.01 cr [F] (PPT Jun 2026), and cumulative five-year free cash flow of -Rs 37 cr [F] (NUMBERS). Every rupee of reported profit over five years has been consumed, and then some, by the cycle.

**The offsetting factor:** the company is debt-free with equity at 77.2% of the balance sheet [E] (PPT Jun 2026), so it has borrowing capacity it did not have in FY24. If the partnerships are non-exclusive and terminable, the score for regulatory barriers and switching costs is materially overstated; if they are long and exclusive, it is understated. **We cannot tell, and the difference is the difference between a 3.9 and a 5.5** [AI].

**2. Does qualification convert into repeat revenue, or only into repeat bidding?** The entire switching-cost argument rests on the proposition that a qualified installed base generates upgrades, spares and repeat orders [F] (PPT Jun 2026). The company has never published a repeat-order rate, a spares or service revenue line, an installed-base count, or a single example of a replacement order won. Meanwhile management describes the government business as competitively re-tendered each time, with L1 status unknown until bid opening [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). **If qualification only buys the right to bid again, the switching-cost score should be closer to 3 than 6** [AI].

blocks.text: **Admach has a position, not a moat.** The position is real: a qualified, lower-cost domestic alternative to European suppliers in a technically demanding niche, reinforced by local-content policy and by partnerships that give it capability it could not build alone. Over a three to five year horizon that position is likely to hold, because qualification cycles are slow and because no evidenced domestic end-to-end competitor has emerged [AI].

But a moat is what prevents competitors from capturing the economics of growth, and on the evidence available nothing here does that. There is no owned technology, no contract longer than a purchase order, no pricing power visible in a roughly 30% gross margin that has not expanded in two years, no customer that cannot re-tender, and a receivable cycle that has lengthened every year for five years - the classic signature of a supplier that accepts terms rather than sets them [F] (NUMBERS) [E]. **At a price implying 56.8% compound sales growth for five years [F] (NUMBERS), the moat question is not academic: sustaining that growth requires a durable competitive advantage that the evidence does not currently support** [AI].

blocks.text: **Supply-side concentration: not disclosed and not inferable.** No document available to us describes the structure of the Indian SPM or industrial NDT industry, its fragmentation, its number of participants or any market-share data. The only structural assertion is management's, that the credible competition is European [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

**Demand-side concentration is high and is a feature of the industry, not of the company.** The buyers are integrated steel producers, state defence and nuclear undertakings, and global machine builders - a small number of large, sophisticated, price-disciplined counterparties with long procurement cycles and, in the government case, statutory L1 tendering [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). **Channel structure has three routes,** all of which the company uses: direct domestic sales to steel and industrial buyers; competitive government tenders where award is on lowest price and status is unknown until bid opening [MC] (CALL Feb 2026); and the European partner channel, where Admach either manufactures equipment the partner sells globally under its own channels, or bids jointly with the partner to satisfy local-content rules [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Feb 2026). **The share of revenue flowing through each route is not disclosed** - which matters, because the three routes have materially different margin, working-capital and durability characteristics [AI].

**Margin driver.** A flat 19% EBITDA margin throughout. The model gives no credit to the 300-400 basis points management expects from backward integration [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), and equally no credit to the 15.05% margin excluding other income at which the business exited H2 FY26 [E].

**Cash driver, and the reason FCFF is so small early.** At 151 working-capital days, every rupee of incremental sales absorbs roughly 41 paise of working capital, so FY27 free cash flow is only Rs 1.1 cr on Rs 17.0 cr of EBITDA [F] (NUMBERS) [E]. **This is the model faithfully reproducing the central problem of the business.** Cash flow only becomes meaningful in FY30-FY31 as growth fades and the working-capital build slows.

**Terminal value dominance.** Rs 97.5 cr of the Rs 117.7 cr enterprise value - **82.8% - is terminal value** [E] (NUMBERS). Only 17.2% of the base-case value comes from the five years actually forecast. That is a structural feature of valuing a growth business on a fade model, and it means the answer is far more sensitive to the WACC and terminal-growth assumptions than to anything in the explicit forecast [AI].
**Value per share** is driven by equity value divided by 0.678 cr shares - with no debt, enterprise value equals equity value [F] (NUMBERS).
**Enterprise value** = present value of five years of FCFF (Rs 20.3 cr, 17.2%) + present value of terminal value (Rs 97.5 cr, 82.8%) [F] (NUMBERS) [E].

**FCFF each year** = EBITDA - tax on EBIT - capex - change in net working capital [F] (NUMBERS). At 19% margins and 151 working-capital days, growth is close to self-cancelling in cash terms for the first two years.
**EBITDA** = sales x 19%. Sales is the only variable driving it; there is no operating-leverage assumption in the model [F] (NUMBERS).

**Sales** = Rs 69 cr compounding at a rate fading 30% to 10% [F] (NUMBERS). This is the variable to which the explicit-period value is most sensitive, and it maps directly onto the order book, which is the observable the company actually publishes.

**Terminal value** = FY31 FCFF grown at 5.5% and capitalised at (15.0% - 5.5%) [F] (NUMBERS). Because this is 82.8% of the answer, **the practical driver tree for the base case is: WACC, terminal growth, and the FY31 cash flow level** - not the year-by-year growth path [AI].

subsections.title: What the forecast deliberately does not assume

items: **It does not assume the working-capital improvement management guides to.** At 151 days the model is already more optimistic than FY26's 231 days, but far less optimistic than the 75 days management targets for FY27 [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). If management delivered 75 days, free cash flow would be materially higher than modelled; if 231 days persists, materially lower. **We do not produce either alternative figure.**
**It does not assume margin expansion.** No credit for backward integration, no credit for a defence and nuclear mix shift, no operating leverage [F] (NUMBERS).

**It does not assume any new order.** The Rs 200 cr quotation pipeline, the four to eight NFC follow-on projects, the 155 mm howitzer opportunity and the bright-bar product entry are all absent from the model - they are embedded only to the extent the fading growth rate implicitly covers them [AI].

**It does not assume Unit 2 or Unit 3.** FY31 sales of Rs 170.2 cr sit below management's Rs 200 cr stated ceiling for the existing facility [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), so no second-site capex or funding is contemplated.
**It does not assume any dividend, buyback or further equity issuance** [F] (NUMBERS).
**It does not assume the FY26 tax rate persists.** The model uses 25.2% against a FY26 effective rate of 16.89% [F] (NUMBERS) [E].

**It does not apply a liquidity or small-company discount**, despite same-day traded turnover of about Rs 25.21 lakh [F] (BOARD). An investor who believes such a discount is warranted should regard the modelled values as before any such adjustment [AI].

blocks.text: **Note the counter-intuitive line: the bull case has negative free cash flow in year one and the bear case has the highest year-one free cash flow of the three** [F] (NUMBERS). That is not a modelling error - it is the arithmetic of a working-capital-intensive business. Faster growth consumes more working capital and more capex, so in the near term growth destroys cash and stagnation releases it. **This is the single most important thing the scenario table tells an investor about Admach**, and it is the same mechanism that produced -Rs 4.53 cr of operating cash flow in FY26 on Rs 10.01 cr of reported profit [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [AI].

**We do not assign numerical probabilities.** The evidence base does not support that degree of precision: there is no annual report, no customer concentration data, no segment margins, no ageing schedule and only four half-year reporting periods in the record. What we can do is rank the scenarios by how much of each depends on things that have already happened versus things that have not.

items: **The bear case requires nothing new to happen.** 12% starting growth and a 15% EBITDA margin are close to what the business actually did in the most recent reporting half: H2 FY26 grew 27% year on year but carried a 15.05% margin excluding other income [E] (PPT Jun 2026). A 15% margin is the H2 FY26 exit rate. **The bear scenario is approximately the current run-rate extended.** That does not make it likely; it makes it the least demanding of the three.

**The base case requires the order book to grow.** 30% growth in FY27 means about Rs 89.7 cr of revenue against an opening order book of roughly Rs 65-68 cr that management says will be consumed by end-September 2026 [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS). It also requires the 19% margin to hold against a 15.05% exit rate [E]. Both are plausible and neither is evidenced yet.

**The bull case requires three things simultaneously:** 43.5% growth in FY27 (above management's own 'easily pass Rs 100 crores'), a 21% EBITDA margin the company has never achieved for a full year [F] (NUMBERS), and by FY31 a revenue level 18% above the maximum management says the existing facility can support [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). It is not impossible - Unit 2 and Unit 3 land exists - but each additional condition compounds.

**Our qualitative weighting:** the base case is the most defensible central expectation; the bear case is materially more likely than a conventional bear case would be, because it requires only continuation of the latest reported half; and the bull case requires a conjunction of three improvements, none of which is yet visible in reported numbers [AI].

subsections.title: Multiples against the disclosed peer set

blocks.text: **No peer comparison is possible in this report, because no peer set is disclosed.** The investor presentation contains no benchmarking page, neither earnings call names a single competing company, and no prospectus is in our evidence set [F] (PPT Jun 2026) (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Jun 2026). We therefore make no relative multiple comparison - not to listed automation names, not to defence suppliers, not to capital-goods peers. **Any peer multiple an investor encounters for this name has not come from the company's own disclosure**, and given that management characterises its competition as European rather than Indian [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), the choice of an Indian listed comparable set would itself be an unsupported analytical judgement [AI].

What can be said without a peer set is how the multiples relate to the company's own economics. At 32.2x trailing earnings and 24.8x trailing EBITDA [F] (NUMBERS), the shares are capitalising a profit stream that has never converted into cash - operating cash flow has been -0.58x profit over three years and free cash flow has been negative in all five [F] (NUMBERS). At 4.57x book [F] (NUMBERS), they are capitalising a net worth of which Rs 11.44 cr is capital work in progress that earned nothing in FY26 and Rs 6.14 cr is unexplained long-term advances - together 23.1% of book value having generated no return [E] (PPT Jun 2026). At 4.67x sales [F] (NUMBERS), they are capitalising a revenue line with a roughly 30% gross margin and a 166-day receivable cycle [E] (NUMBERS).

subsections.title: Interpreting the DCF and its assumptions

items: **All three scenario values sit below the current price, and so does the entire sensitivity grid.** Bear Rs 89.2, base Rs 173.6, bull Rs 258.3, against Rs 475 - implying -81.2%, -63.5% and -45.6% respectively [F] (NUMBERS). The best cell in the WACC and terminal-growth grid is Rs 232.2 [F] (NUMBERS). **This is an unusually clean result: there is no interior assumption within the tested ranges that reconciles the model to the market.**

**Where the model is conservative.** It uses a 25.2% tax rate against a FY26 effective rate of 16.89% [F] (NUMBERS) [E]. It charges capex on a 10x fixed-asset turnover against an actual 13.8x [F] (NUMBERS). It gives no credit for backward integration, for the defence and nuclear pipeline, for the Rs 200 cr quotation book, or for the Rs 11.44 cr of CWIP that has not yet started producing. It applies a 15% WACC to a debt-free company [F] (NUMBERS).

**Where the model is generous.** It assumes a 19% EBITDA margin against a 15.05% H2 FY26 exit rate excluding other income [E]. It assumes 151 working-capital days against 231 actual [F] (NUMBERS). It assumes 5.5% terminal growth in perpetuity for a sub-scale, single-site, project-based business [AI]. And 82.8% of the base-case value rests on that terminal assumption [E].

**Where the model is silent.** It contains no liquidity discount, despite same-day turnover of about Rs 25.21 lakh [F] (BOARD); no key-man discount, despite a promoter-led board with no named CFO [F] (PPT Jun 2026); and no discount for the disclosure gaps documented throughout this report [AI].

**The honest summary:** the DCF is neither a bull nor a bear document. Its central assumptions are close to what the company has actually reported over the last two years, and on those assumptions the modelled value is well below the traded price. **The gap is not a modelling artefact; it is the question the investor has to answer** [AI].

blocks.text: **The key forensic conclusion.** The price requires 56.8% compound sales growth for five years [F] (NUMBERS). That is **2.9 times the base case, 2.0 times the bull case, and would take revenue to roughly Rs 654 cr by FY31 - about 3.3 times the Rs 200 cr that management itself says is the maximum the existing facility can produce, and 3.3 times the Rs 200 cr they aspire to reach by FY28** [E] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). To be clear about what that means: an investor buying at Rs 475 is not underwriting management's plan. They are underwriting roughly three times management's plan, executed from a site management says caps out at Rs 200 cr, funded by a business that has never generated free cash flow, with an order book of Rs 68.37 cr [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS) (NUMBERS).

The comparison to the company's own 74.4% three-year historical growth [F] (NUMBERS) is the obvious bull rejoinder and it does not survive contact with the base. That 74.4% was compounded from Rs 13 cr in FY23 - a year in which revenue actually fell from Rs 14 cr [F] (NUMBERS). Compounding 56.8% from Rs 69 cr requires adding roughly Rs 585 cr of annual revenue over five years, against Rs 56 cr added over the last three [E]. **Growth rates off a Rs 13 cr base carry no information about what is achievable off a Rs 69 cr base, particularly in a business that consumes 63 paise of working capital per rupee of annual revenue** [E] [AI].

The bear reading above rests on a model, and the model can be challenged on four defensible grounds. **First, the discount rate.** A 15% WACC with a 7% equity risk premium and a 1.15 beta is a reasonable generic input, but it is applied to a debt-free company with 77% equity funding, high returns on capital and no refinancing risk [F] (NUMBERS) (PPT Jun 2026). At a 13.5% WACC the base value rises to Rs 199-232 [F] (NUMBERS) - still below the price, but the direction is instructive.

**Second, the working-capital assumption penalises growth twice.** The model charges 151 working-capital days against every rupee of incremental sales, which is why bull-case year-one free cash flow is negative [F] (NUMBERS). If backward integration genuinely cuts 30-60 days from each project's build cycle [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) and the cycle moves towards management's 75-day target, the cash profile of the growth years changes materially - and the model would be penalising the company for a problem it is actively fixing. **We do not compute that alternative value**; we note that the assumption is contested by management in the company's favour, and that it has not been delivered in any year.

**Third, a five-year FCFF fade is an awkward frame for an option-like exposure.** Admach's defence, nuclear and European-partner positions have the character of options: low current value, binary conversion, and payoffs that a linear fade model cannot capture. A Rs 10 cr Nuclear Fuel Complex order with four to eight identified follow-ons [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), if it converted into a programme relationship, would not look like 19.8% fading growth. **Fourth, a flat 19% margin assumes no operating leverage whatsoever** on a business that has nearly doubled revenue in two years while holding margin - which arguably understates what scale should do to a fixed overhead base of Rs 8.15 cr [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [AI].

**Where the counter-argument stops.** Each of these four points moves the modelled value upward, and the sensitivity grid already tests the first: even at a 13.5% WACC with 6.5% terminal growth, the base case reaches Rs 232.2 - 51.1% below the traded price [E] (NUMBERS). The remaining three would have to move the value by more than 100% together. **The honest statement is that the counter-arguments are real and directionally correct, and that closing a gap of this size requires all of them to be right simultaneously and by a large margin** [AI].

blocks.text: **Simple average: 3.3 out of 10. This is not a rating and implies no recommendation.** The distribution is the message: one factor scores 7 (balance sheet), two score 6 and 5 (capacity optionality, growth durability), and the two valuation factors score 1 each. **Strip out the two valuation lines and the average of the thirteen business-quality factors is 3.7** [E] - a modest business-quality score on its own terms, before any consideration of price. The scorecard says the same thing as the DCF from a different direction: the issue here is not only what you pay, it is also what you are told before you pay it.

Admach is a genuine engineering business, not a listing vehicle. It designs and builds special purpose machines that X-ray assembled howitzer shells, condition alloy billets for Tata Steel, and inspect API-standard pipe for oil and gas customers - work that requires qualification into supply chains that are slow and expensive to enter [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Its managing director answers technical questions with a specificity that is difficult to manufacture, and declines to size his own addressable market when invited to inflate it [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). It has real customers with real names: Tata Steel, NMDC Steel, Nuclear Fuel Complex, ArcelorMittal, Indian Ordnance Factories, six European machine builders.

The financial case is that it nearly quadrupled revenue in three years while holding operating margin at roughly 19-20%, cleared all its debt, and now sits on a balance sheet that is 77% equity-funded with capacity management says supports three times current revenue [F] (NUMBERS) (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). It sits in front of three policy-supported demand streams - defence indigenisation, the nuclear build-out, and the relocation of European engineering supply chains to India - and it participates in all three through partnerships and qualifications that already exist rather than through ambition [F] (PPT Jun 2026). Its capex programme was delivered on schedule, and the operating benefit of that programme has not yet appeared in any reported number, which is either a disappointment or an unbanked asset [AI].

The strongest single argument for owning it is the one the model cannot capture: a four-to-eight project Nuclear Fuel Complex pipeline at roughly Rs 10 cr each, a 155 mm shell inspection capability that has already been exported to three governments, and a European partner network entering what management calls Phase 2 - joint export rather than inbound technology - are option-like exposures on a Rs 322 cr market capitalisation [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [F] (NUMBERS). A five-year FCFF fade model prices none of that [AI].

The case against is arithmetic, and it is unusually clean. Every scenario value in our model and every cell of the sensitivity grid sits below the traded price: bear Rs 89.2, base Rs 173.6, bull Rs 258.3, best grid cell Rs 232.2, against Rs 475 [F] (NUMBERS) [E]. The reverse DCF says the price requires 56.8% compound sales growth for five years [F] (NUMBERS) - roughly Rs 654 cr of revenue by FY31, about 3.3 times the maximum management says the existing facility can produce [E] [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

Underneath the valuation sit three operating facts. **The company has never generated free cash flow** - negative in all five disclosed years, cumulative -Rs 37 cr, with operating cash flow at -0.58x profit over three years [F] (NUMBERS). **The working-capital cycle is widening, not narrowing** - 231 days against an 89-day average, debtor days up in each of the last five years, against a management target of 75 days for FY27 [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). **And the most recent reported half was the weakest in two years on margin** - 15.05% excluding other income against 23.45% in the preceding half [E].

Around those sit the disclosure problems: no customer concentration data in any year, no segment margins, no related-party schedule, no contingent liabilities, no auditor's report, no prospectus, a promised segment disclosure not delivered, two consecutive announcements publishing contradictory order-book figures, a published cash-flow column that does not balance, and an unexplained H2 tax rate that management was asked about twice and did not answer [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS) [E] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Add institutions exiting from 10.78% to 2.06% within one quarter of listing, a shareholder count halving to 417, and same-day traded turnover of about Rs 25 lakh [F] (NUMBERS) (BOARD).

subsections.title: What the market may be missing, in both directions

items: **Missing on the bull side:** the European partner channel. Six partnerships, three added in 2025, that supply technology inbound and distribution outbound, and that make Admach the default Indian integrator when a 50% local-content rule forces a European principal to partner rather than bid [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). This is the most durable and least discussed part of the business, and it is entirely absent from the presentation's own investment rationale framing, which leads with defence and nuclear TAM instead [AI].

**Missing on the bull side:** the FY24 margin reset is a feature, not a warning. The market may be reading 32% to 19% as deterioration. Management has explained it as the normalisation of a single Tata Steel project, and the business has since held 19-20% while nearly doubling revenue [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [F] (NUMBERS). That is a stronger operating record than the headline decline suggests [AI].

**Missing on the bear side:** growth in this business consumes cash rather than producing it. Our own model makes the point unusually clearly - bull-case year-one free cash flow is negative while bear-case year-one free cash flow is the highest of the three [F] (NUMBERS). Investors extrapolating 29% revenue growth and 59% profit growth may not have noticed that FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs 4.53 cr [F] (PPT Jun 2026).

**Missing on the bear side:** the defence and nuclear exposure is roughly one seventh of revenue, not the business. The presentation devotes six of thirty pages to defence and nuclear industry data and none of them contains an Admach number; management's own figure is 10-15% of H1 FY26 revenue [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). The narrative weight and the revenue weight are very different things [AI].

**Missing on both sides:** nobody has asked about the Rs 6.14 cr of long-term loans and advances that appeared from nothing in FY26 [F] (PPT Jun 2026). It is either a mundane capital advance - in which case one sentence resolves it - or it is not [AI].

blocks.text: **Every reference point available - all three DCF scenarios, every cell of the sensitivity grid, book value, the IPO issue price and the 52-week low - sits below the current price.** We present this framing without a rating and without a price target. What it establishes is narrow but firm: an investor buying at Rs 475 is not buying at a discount to any value benchmark our evidence base supports, and is therefore relying entirely on outcomes materially better than the bull case [AI].

items: **The good outcome.** The working-capital cycle halves as backward integration cuts 30-60 days per project; FY27 delivers above Rs 100 cr with a 20%-plus margin and the first positive operating cash flow in the company's history; four NFC repeat orders convert; the European partnerships enter Phase 2 exports; Unit 2 is built on transferred land; revenue reaches Rs 200-235 cr by FY30-FY31, in line with the bull projection [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The business would then be a genuinely good one - and the bull-case value would still be Rs 258.3 per share [F] (NUMBERS).

**The likely middle.** Revenue compounds in the high teens to low twenties, margin oscillates between 15% and 20% with order mix, working capital improves modestly but never reaches 75 days, operating cash flow turns positive in some years and negative in others, and the company periodically raises working-capital debt. Revenue reaches Rs 150-180 cr by FY31, close to the base projection of Rs 170.2 cr [F] (NUMBERS) [AI].

**The bad outcome.** A steel capex pause or a slipped defence cycle leaves the order book below Rs 50 cr; the newly in-sourced fixed cost base becomes a drag at lower utilisation; receivables require provisioning; the company raises equity at a lower price to fund the cycle. Revenue stalls near Rs 100 cr, close to the bear projection of Rs 103.6 cr [F] (NUMBERS) [AI].

**The tail outcome nobody models.** A single-site manufacturer with Rs 28.24 cr of inventory and 20-25 live projects at one Pune address, with no disclosed insurance or business-continuity arrangement [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Low probability, high severity, and entirely absent from every valuation in this report [AI].

**What links all four:** in none of them does revenue reach the roughly Rs 654 cr by FY31 that the current price implies [E] (NUMBERS). The possibility space and the priced expectation do not overlap on our evidence.

subsections.title: Where the price sits against the modelled values

blocks.text: **We issue no rating and no price target.** The research view is this. Admach Systems is a real, capable, niche engineering business with credible customers, genuine qualification barriers, a debt-free balance sheet and exposure to three policy-supported demand streams. It is also a business that has never generated free cash flow, whose working-capital cycle has widened every year for five years, whose most recent reported half was its weakest on margin in two years, and about which the most basic quality-of-revenue disclosures - customer concentration, segment margins, receivable ageing, related-party transactions - do not exist in the evidence available to us.

At Rs 475 the shares trade above every value reference our evidence supports: 174% above the base-case value of Rs 173.6, 84% above the bull-case value of Rs 258.3, 105% above the most favourable cell of the sensitivity grid at Rs 232.2, 357% above book value of Rs 104, and 99% above the Rs 239 IPO price of nine months ago [F] (NUMBERS) (BOARD) [E]. The reverse DCF frames the gap most usefully: the price requires about 57% compound sales growth for five years against 20% in the base case and about 28% in the bull case [F] (NUMBERS) [E].

items: **A narrative-to-revenue mismatch.** The defence, nuclear and aerospace story that dominates the investor presentation is, on management's own figures, 10-15% of revenue [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [F] (PPT Jun 2026). Six of thirty presentation pages carry industry TAM with no Admach number on any of them.
**A profit-to-cash mismatch.** Reported PAT grew 59% in FY26 while operating cash flow was -Rs 4.53 cr [F] (PPT Jun 2026). The market is capitalising the first number.

**Scarcity and float dynamics.** 417 shareholders, same-day turnover of about Rs 25 lakh, and a 165% rise from the 52-week low [F] (NUMBERS) (BOARD). Thin float can sustain a price well above fundamental anchors for extended periods - in either direction [AI].

**Genuine, unmodelled optionality.** The nuclear pipeline and the European Phase 2 export plan are real and a fade model cannot price them [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Some part of the gap is a legitimate option premium; we do not believe it is 174% of base-case value [AI].

**An evidence vacuum that cuts both ways.** With no annual report, no prospectus and no peer disclosure available, there is little to anchor a price to. Absence of disclosure removes the friction that normally corrects an over- or under-valuation [AI].

The operating thesis - backward integration lifting margin, working capital normalising, order conversion accelerating - needs two to three years and four to six reporting periods to prove out. **Anyone taking a position should expect to hold through at least FY28 and should size it against confirmed same-day turnover of about Rs 25 lakh** [F] (BOARD), which is a hard constraint, not an inconvenience [AI].
