blocks.text: **The single sentence version.** Admach is a real business at an early stage of a genuine opportunity, reported by a finance function that has not yet caught up with its listed status, trading at a price that requires roughly three times what its own management says its factory can produce. The business is worth following closely; the disclosure gaps are worth closing before acting; and the gap between the price and every value benchmark in our evidence base is worth resolving in the investor's own mind before, not after, taking a position.

**This is initial coverage.** No previous report exists for Admach Systems in our evidence set, so there is no prior quarter's numbers, disclosures, guidance items, risks or thesis to compare against. The company listed on the BSE SME platform on 31 December 2025 [F] (BOARD) and has held two investor calls and published one investor presentation since [F] (CALL Feb 2026) (CALL Jun 2026) (PPT Jun 2026), which is the entire post-listing disclosure record available to us alongside four exchange announcements and the screener statements data. In place of a quarter-on-quarter comparison, we have tested every guidance statement made on the January 2026 call against the audited FY26 outcome - set out in full in the guidance tracker - and we have documented thirteen inconsistencies across the four documents in the financial forensics section, both of which serve the same purpose for a first review. **From the next review onwards, the testable items are the five falsifiable claims management made on 28 May 2026: FY27 revenue above Rs 100 cr, FY27 EBITDA margin above 20%, FY27 working-capital days of about 75, positive FY27 operating cash flow, and completion of the Rs 65 cr order book by end-September 2026** [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

blocks.caption: Second-pass checks
rows: All industry figures are confined to class F of the order-book classification and to the industry structure section, and are explicitly labelled as context. Illustrative share arithmetic is labelled [E] and framed as showing scale, not forecasting share. We also recorded that the MD himself declined to size the TAM
Order book and pipeline conflation avoided

The mandatory A-F table separates recognised revenue, contracted backlog, qualified opportunity, tender pipeline, management aspiration and industry TAM. The Rs 200 cr quotation book is kept in class D throughout and never added to the order book
Management claims labelled and separated from fact

Every management statement carries [MC] with the call date. Where an analyst asserted a figure that management neither confirmed nor corrected - the 5% defence share, the Rs 15 cr capex framing, the RHP 100% utilisation point - we flagged the attribution as uncertain rather than treating it as a company claim

We show the improving case (widening named customer base, rising export mix, management's diversification account) and the worsening case (Rs 15-16 cr single machine at 22% of revenue, single-counterparty nuclear pipeline, FY24 Tata Steel dominance). **The evidence is thin because the company discloses no concentration data at all - we state this rather than fill the gap**
Cash flow and working capital completeness

Five years of CFO, CFI, CFF and FCF; CFO/PAT by year and cumulative; full working-capital component build; net operating working capital computed from the balance sheet; the FY24 CFO discrepancy between sources shown side by side and not reconciled
Current share count and market capitalisation used

0.678 cr shares and Rs 322 cr market capitalisation at Rs 475 throughout [F] (NUMBERS). We explicitly flagged that the investor presentation's Rs 250 price and Rs 169.32 cr market capitalisation are as at 22 May 2026 and must not be mixed with the current basis

Each year's margin move is classified explicitly in the margin analysis; bull drivers are classified structural, company-specific or cyclical in the executive summary; structural themes are split into supported and unsupported
All eight carry numeric thresholds tied to a specific reporting period - working-capital days above 180, FY27 revenue below Rs 85 cr, order book below Rs 60 cr, top customer above 30%, and so on

No customer, contract, order, capacity figure, market share, guidance item or date has been invented. Where a figure is not disclosed we say so - customer concentration, segment margins, contingent liabilities, related-party transactions, import dependence, currency exposure, lock-in dates, pledges, auditor identity and peer set are all recorded as not disclosed

Every factual and analytical statement carries exactly one of [F], [MC], [AI] or [E]. **Caveat: the geography percentages taken from the presentation's stacked-bar chart are labelled [F] but rest on our reading of chart labels, and the FY25 column sums to 99.54% rather than 100% in our copy. We flagged this inline rather than suppressing the data**

Thirteen inconsistencies are tabulated side by side in the financial forensics section, including the FY24 cash-flow sign flip, the non-balancing FY24 columns, the FY24 EPS, the July-August order book contradiction, the export country count, the years-in-business claim, the land area and the Taiwan attribution

Every valuation figure comes from our DCF model: scenario values, projections, the sensitivity grid, the reverse DCF and the upside percentages. **No new fair value, multiple or target has been produced.** The two derived figures - the implied FY31 revenue of about Rs 654 cr and the bull and bear five-year CAGRs - are arithmetic on model outputs and are labelled [E] with their basis stated
Bull case tested against the reverse DCF

The priced-in section sets the 56.8% implied CAGR against the bull case's approximately 27.8%, against management's own Rs 200 cr facility ceiling, and against the Rs 654 cr FY31 revenue the price implies. The strongest counter-argument is given its own subsection and is not strawmanned

An eight-row bull table with evidence and confidence ratings, eleven numbered bear points, three two-sided key debates plus two further debates, a variant perception, and a final thesis that argues both sides and identifies what the market may be missing in each direction

No buy, sell, hold, overweight or underweight appears anywhere; no price target is given. The investment scorecard is explicitly labelled an assessment framework and not a rating. No marketing adjectives are used to describe the company

In order of materiality: (1) no annual report text, so no auditor's report, CARO, key audit matters, related-party schedule, contingent liabilities or receivable ageing; (2) no prospectus, so no pre-IPO capital history, lock-in dates or peer comparison; (3) no customer concentration data in any year; (4) no segment margins or segment rupee revenue; (5) the presentation's segment mix chart is not legible in our copy; (6) shareholding data stops at March 2026, two quarters stale; (7) no import dependence, currency exposure or tariff disclosure. **Several conclusions in this report are therefore provisional on documents we could not read, and we have said so at each point rather than only here**

summary.one_line: Admach Systems is a genuine, newly listed Pune special-purpose-machine and NDT builder with credible customers, zero debt and real defence, nuclear and European-partner optionality, but it has never generated free cash flow, its working-capital cycle has widened every year for five years, its most recent half was its weakest on margin in two years, and at Rs 475 the shares trade above every value benchmark our evidence supports - including the bull case - on a price that implies roughly 57% compound sales growth for five years against management's own Rs 200 cr facility ceiling.
bull_points: Debt-free balance sheet with real capacity headroom: borrowings fell from Rs 16 cr (FY24) to nil at 31 March 2026, equity funds 77.2% of assets, interest cover is 13x, and only 28,925 sq ft of 75,347 sq ft of land is utilised, with further land held for Units 2 and 3. [F] (NUMBERS) (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

Margin normalised rather than deteriorated, and has held through rapid growth: after the FY24 operating margin of 32% - which the Company Secretary attributed to a single Tata Steel project - the business held roughly 19-20% operating margin in both FY25 and FY26 while revenue rose from Rs 19.68 cr to Rs 68.91 cr. [F] (NUMBERS) (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Six European technology partnerships - VisiConsult, Braun Maschinenfabrik, SAS Engineering & Planning, Surface Engineering, Nordinkraft and Sofratest - give access to NDT and steel-processing technology a Rs 69 cr company could not develop alone, and make Admach the default Indian integrator when a 50% Make-in-India local-content rule forces European principals to partner rather than bid directly. [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

A named, specific nuclear and defence pipeline exists rather than being asserted: a live Rs 10 cr Nuclear Fuel Complex order executable by September 2026, with four to eight similar follow-on projects at technical-offer stage, alongside shell and missile-body inspection systems already supplied to Indian Ordnance Factories and exported to government buyers in Korea, Brazil and Taiwan. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Feb 2026) [F] (PPT Jun 2026)

Export mix is rising fast off a near-zero base - international revenue was 0.06% of FY24, 7.16% of FY25 and 12.61% of FY26 - with six direct-export pipe projects for a US customer under execution and management stating that export margins are higher than domestic. [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)
bear_points: The company has never generated free cash flow. Operating cash flow was -0.58x reported profit over three years and -0.74x over five; free cash flow was negative in all five disclosed years, cumulatively -Rs 37 cr; FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs 4.53 cr against PAT of Rs 10.01 cr. [F] (NUMBERS) [E] (PPT Jun 2026)

Working capital is widening, not narrowing: 231 working-capital days against an 89-day prior average, a 322-day cash conversion cycle, and debtor days rising in each of the last five years to 166 - against which management guides to about 75 days in FY27 and separately claimed an investment cycle of 'not more than 60 days'. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) (CALL Feb 2026)

The price requires roughly three times management's own plan. The reverse DCF implies about 56.8% compound sales growth for five years against 19.8% in the base case and about 27.8% in the bull case - roughly Rs 654 cr of FY31 revenue, about 3.3x the Rs 200 cr management says the existing facility can produce. All three scenario values (Rs 89.2, Rs 173.6, Rs 258.3) and every cell of the sensitivity grid (Rs 139.0 to Rs 232.2) sit below Rs 475. [F] (NUMBERS) [E] [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

The margin exit rate is well below the headline: operating margin excluding other income fell from 23.45% in H1 FY26 to 15.05% in H2 FY26, and roughly Rs 1.7 cr - about 17% - of FY26 PAT came from other income and a lower effective tax rate versus FY25, with the H2 current tax rate of 8.8% challenged twice on the call and left unexplained. [E] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Disclosure gaps and inconsistencies are material: no customer concentration data for any year, no segment margins, no related-party schedule, no contingent liabilities, no auditor's report and no prospectus in our evidence base; an order book reported as rising to Rs 83.77 cr on 16 July 2026 and rising to Rs 68.37 cr on 18 August 2026; an FY24 cash-flow column that does not balance to its own cash movement; institutions exiting from 10.78% to 2.06% within one quarter of listing with the shareholder count halving to 417; and confirmed same-day traded turnover of about Rs 25.21 lakh. [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS) (NUMBERS) (BOARD) [E] (PPT Jun 2026)
watch_points: H1 FY27 results (six months to 30 September 2026): revenue against Rs 28.45 cr in H1 FY26, and operating margin excluding other income against 23.45% in H1 FY26 and 15.05% in H2 FY26 - the first clean test of whether the backward-integration benefit is real. [E] (PPT Jun 2026)

Working capital and receivables at 30 September 2026: debtor days against 166 and working-capital days against 231, as the first measurable step towards management's stated FY27 target of about 75 days. [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

The order book figure published with the next Regulation 30 order announcement - both its absolute level against Rs 68.37 cr at 18 August 2026, and whether it is reported on a basis consistent with the previous release after the July-August contradiction. [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS)

Conversion of the named pipeline: any Nuclear Fuel Complex repeat order from the four to eight projects at technical-offer stage, and any 155 mm howitzer shell order - management's stated one-to-three-month closing window from 28 May 2026 has already lapsed without an announcement. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [AI] (ANNOUNCEMENTS)

The FY26 annual report filed on 31 August 2026 and the 28 September 2026 AGM: auditor's opinion, key audit matters, CARO observations, related-party schedule, contingent liabilities and performance guarantees, receivable ageing, and the nature of the Rs 6.14 cr of long-term loans and advances that appeared in FY26. [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS) (PPT Jun 2026)
guidance: FY27 revenue: 'I'll start from the past. We grew from INR 19 to INR 53, INR 53 to INR 70 crores and this year we will easily pass INR 100 crores.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)
FY28 revenue: asked whether Rs 200 cr by FY28 is fair given the stated facility peak, management replied 'Yes. We are hopeful and confident also.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

FY27 EBITDA margin: 'FY27 company is targeting for 20% to -- above 20%. So, it's a major contribution will be our capex that which will helps to reduce the working capital.' Asked again, 'So, we are pretty confident of this 20% EBITDA? - Yes, for sure.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Margin uplift from backward integration: 'we can say that about 3% to 4% of change in EBITDA margin will be reflecting in in next books or next results. Because we will be saving lot of transportation and payouts to vendors.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

In-house versus outsourced mix: previously 30% in-house and 70% outsourced; 'with all these machines installed in-house, this will be flipped, like 30% outsourced and 70% in-house.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)
FY27 working-capital days: asked what working capital days should be in FY27 given the current mix of orders, management replied 'About 75.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)
Working capital required at scale: 'for INR 200 crores revenue, we will need INR 20 to INR 30 crores. That that's enough.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)
Operating cash flow: 'I think in the next year we can say that the operations cash flow from operations will be positive side.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Order book and its execution: order book of approximately Rs 65 cr ('INR 64 crores point something, INR65 crores I would say'), and 'This INR 65 crores order book will be completed by end of September or maybe half month, the next half month.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026) [F] (PPT Jun 2026)

Quotation pipeline and conversion: 'the offers which have gone to our customers with the current scenario are of the tune of more than INR200 crores, which we have already quoted. And if I can tell you on thumb rule, the conversion rates are about 60%-65%.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Defence order conversion: on 155 mm howitzer shell inquiries, 'the things are in quite advanced discussions, and should get closed in next one or two months or maybe maximum three months.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Nuclear pipeline: 'we have an order from Nuclear Fuel Complex for INR10 crores currently, which will be executed maybe by end of September. And we are expecting about four to eight more similar projects from the same company and the technical offers are already submitted to them... those orders will come for sure.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Capacity: 'we are currently at let's say INR 70 crores revenue. This facility, current facility, we can easily cater to about INR 200 crores', with land already purchased so that 'we can immediately go for Unit 2, Unit 3 immediately.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

FY27 capex: 'Currently I don't foresee any capex investment immediately, but if it comes to some specific project where we can increase our margin or save our times or save our overheads, for sure we will go for it.' Two remaining machines were stated to be arriving from vendors by July 2026. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

New products: on bright bar and superfinishing, 'we have already initiated our operations, design, everything for making machines in the bright bar and superfinishing areas... our next target or rather already under execution is in the bright bar side.' No plan to enter the hot side of steel. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)
Dividend: asked about dividends given no immediate capex, management replied 'it is under discussion with our team. It is under discussion.' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Segment disclosure commitment: asked for a revenue bifurcation by product, management said the details would be given to the investor-relations firm 'in next few days' and 'maybe in another week's time' from 28 May 2026. Not delivered in any document available to us. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)
Fund-raising: no post-IPO fund-raising was guided or announced. [F] (CALL Jun 2026) (PPT Jun 2026) (ANNOUNCEMENTS)
Utilisation: no numeric utilisation guidance was given in any period - only the revenue-equivalent capacity claim of Rs 200 cr. [MC] (CALL Jun 2026)

Post-quarter order announcements, for the tracker: Rs 295.73 lakh NDT order with 16-week delivery, order book stated to rise to Rs 83.77 cr (16 July 2026); Rs 159.30 lakh domestic bar handling system order executable in 7 months, order book stated to rise to Rs 68.37 cr (14 and 18 August 2026). [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS)
